svg.text: A drum on one spindle, a coaxial second spindle for heads, and the pair tilts through 360°: pot, wok, peeler, inverter, washer.
drum Ø240 × 200 deep, 7 L, hemispherical floor r = 120
7 actuators per unit · swing circle Ø850

g.text: fin augers food out over the lip

svg.text: ONE UNIT, SIX MACHINES (tilt angle + head)
Heads by the same chuck: scraper, hook, masher grid, blade, whisk,
feed tube + piston (cutting disc on the drum mouth), strainer, lance, lid,
or a second drum / face pan mouth to mouth (flip, clamshell).
weak point: flat and formed food (Schnitzel, Rouladen) go to the face pan;
the 850 mm swing circle is a large, hot, moving assembly

g.text: 1/7 The frame tilts the drum to 45°; the transport tips potatoes into the mouth.
2/7 Rasp-lined drum turns at 55 rpm, water from the lance on spindle 2: a drum peeler.
3/7 Strainer head on the mouth, tilt to 120°: the slurry pours into the drain, the potatoes stay.
4/7 Back to 45°: the curved induction cradle heats while the drum turns — a rotating wok.
5/7 Tilt to 135°, reverse rotation: the fin augers the food out over the lip onto the plate.
6/7 Wash in place: lance inside, drum at 150° turns past fixed jets; water drains out of the mouth.
7/7 Induction heats the wet drum to 105 °C for 30 s: sanitised and dry, ready for the next dish.
